newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Britain's Eastern Group takes 11 pct stake in Czech utility. [CORRECTED 14:55 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Britain's Eastern Group takes 11 pct stake in Czech utility. [CORRECTED 14:55 GMT]

text.p: (Corrects company name and deletes erroneous acronym in headline and first paragraph)
Britain's Eastern Group has taken an 11 percent stake in Czech electricity distributor Severomoravska Energetika, the CTK news agency reported on Thursday.
CTK did not give further details of the sale.
SME officials were not immediately available for comment, but have since confirmed the sale.
SME official Petr Ivanek told Reuters that Eastern bought the stake for 1.5 billion crowns from Czech bank Ceskoslovenska Obchodni Banka a.s..
"They told us they are long-term investors and that they wanted the stake in tandem with Eastern's holding in utility Teplarny Brno a.s.," he said.
Teplarny Brno is a heating utility based in the Czech second city of Brno, about 200 km southeast of Prague.
Industrial conglomerate Hanson recently bought Eastern Electricity, renamed it Eastern Group and aims to spin it off as part of a separate business under its demerger plans.
